web.title: AI Agents Are About to Flood the Workforce. No One's Ready for It
web.description: Your next coworker might well be an AI agent—and will require a whole new model of workplace interactions.

In the coming months, hundreds of thousands of brand-new coworkers will be entering the workforce. You’ll learn their names and recognize their profile pictures. They’ll get added to your email chains and Slack channels. They’ll become chiefs of staff, engineers, and marketing gurus.

But these coworkers aren’t human: They are all [artificial intelligence](https://www.wired.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) agents.

[The rise of AI agents](https://www.wired.com/story/ai-agents-are-thirsty-for-power/)—systems, based on large language models, designed to complete tasks autonomously—has launched a tsunami of companies selling the [services of digital employees](https://www.wired.com/story/all-my-employees-are-ai-agents-so-are-my-executives/). These agents are supposed to be the perfect worker bees: available 24/7, never complaining, and providing superhuman intelligence.

Yet there has been curiously little discussion of what these agents are like as actual coworkers. Julie Bedard, a Boston Consulting Group partner, noticed the murky nature of how people talked about AI at work three years ago, as rapid adoption of [ChatGPT](https://www.wired.com/story/what-openai-really-wants/) convinced executives the technology could bring [exponential improvements in productivity.](https://www.wired.com/story/get-ready-for-the-great-ai-disappointment/)

“People didn't have language for it,” Bedard tells WIRED. “Is it a tool? Is it a teammate? Is it a colleague? Is it a coworker?”

When platforms such as Microsoft’s Copilot and Google’s Gemini for Workspace launched in 2023, they were marketed primarily as tools for employees. But in January, when Bedard and colleagues polled 1,261 managers, 22 percent said their organizations had added AI agents to corporate org charts. Bedard said that this percentage is likely to grow [as dozens of startups](https://www.reddit.com/r/AI_Agents/comments/1tn22qy/i_mapped_100_companies_selling_ai_employees_and/) offer up the services of AI employees and big tech companies hype their autonomous agents. In June, for example, [Microsoft launched “Scout,”](https://www.wired.com/story/meet-microsoft-scout-your-ai-coworker-that-never-logs-off/) an agent built to complete tasks like rescheduling meetings and drafting emails.

“Your company essentially hires your assistant,” Omar Shahine, the corporate vice president of Microsoft Scout, [said when the agent launched.](https://www.wired.com/story/meet-microsoft-scout-your-ai-coworker-that-never-logs-off/) “The whole point of having a personal assistant is that they're working when you're not working.”

The success of AI agents depends not only on their ability to provide financial returns, but also to work harmoniously alongside the existing workforce. That means companies have crafted agents that boast the benefits of AI, packaged in a human-like bundle of traits to encourage employees to anthropomorphize their new colleagues.

“People start to really respect the agent and form strong attachments," says Dhruv Amin, cofounder of Anything, a vibe coding startup that entered the AI coworker market in August with a platform called Skydive. “They'll talk about it like humans.”

Skydive’s agents “aren’t chatbots or workflows,” but coworkers, with their own names, roles, and cloud computers. They work across Slack, email, iMessage, and more. Each is represented by a Muppet-esque avatar, which Amin described as “close to human, but definitely not human.” They have names often related to their roles; Canary, for instance, monitors production 24/7.

“We think it's important to personify them a little bit,” Amin says, “because most people still don't know what a real agent is.”

Christine Wendell, CEO of Pronto Housing and an early Skydive adopter, uses agents for a laundry list of busy work: writing contracts, scheduling meetings, sending follow-ups emails to customers. Her agents are, essentially, perfect employees.

But how are they as coworkers? Skydive agents not only embed in every form of workplace communication, they continually evolve to match coworkers’ communication styles, requests, and corrections. In other words, they become better and better at fitting in with their actual coworkers. When Pronto’s engineering team began using a coding agent, Wendell noticed that employees started saying that they “worked with Alice”—the agent—on a project.

Yet part of the agents’ appeal is that they are not human. Beyond their limitless work ethic, they also exist outside of office politics or professional neuroses. When “Bob,” the agent serving as Wendell’s chief of staff, errantly listed all the details of Wendell’s calendar in a Slack channel, she didn’t feel the need to sugarcoat her swift correction.

“I'm definitely very aware that it's not human,” Wendell says. “I dump on them in a way I wouldn't do to a human, because it would not be polite.”

AI coworkers are entering the job market just as agents are increasingly infiltrating our personal lives. While Silicon Valley has been using [agents such as Open Claw](https://www.wired.com/story/i-gave-my-openclaw-agent-physical-body-robot/) and [Instinct](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/the-latest-viral-ai-assistant-rocketing-across-silicon-valley-abb46276) for months to complete annoying tasks, Meta’s newly launched Muse aims to [push personal AI agents into the mainstream.](https://www.wired.com/story/metas-muse-is-better-at-surveilling-than-helping-me/)

By Lily Hay Newman


Muse, like Skydive’s muppets, is represented by a cute and fuzzy little avatar. In the words of [WIRED senior writer Reece Rogers,](https://www.wired.com/story/metas-muse-is-better-at-surveilling-than-helping-me/) the user experience is something “like texting a friend with task requests—the AI agent acknowledges messages with a thumbs-up emoji and gets to work in the background.” By using existing relationships as a blueprint, these agents—whether they’re AI coworkers or, like Muse, “built for everyone”—offer a shortcut to understanding how to use them.

Anthromorphizing AI comes with specific risks in a work context. Research from Bedard and her colleagues at BCG found that, when managers were told work was completed by an AI employee, they caught 18 percent fewer errors than when told it came from an AI tool. Agents also don’t necessarily fit in the same boxes as human employees, Bedard says, in their abilities or their weaknesses.

“Companies are just starting to wrap their heads around what guardrails” are even applicable, Bedard says.

People forming deep emotional connections with AI is nothing new; people have been [dating chatbot companions for years](https://www.wired.com/story/couples-retreat-with-3-ai-chatbots-and-humans-who-love-them-replika-nomi-chatgpt/) at this point. Even in the workplace, AI tools have sparked some curious reactions. Last year, Henry Blodget—the founder of my former employer, Business Insider—wrote a blog about building a team of digital subordinates, and having a “human response” to the headshot of a particularly attractive AI colleague.

“After a few decades in the human workplace, I’ve learned that sharing certain human thoughts at work is almost always a bad idea,” [Blodget wrote.](https://www.regenerator1.com/p/building-our-native-ai-newsroom) “But did the same rules apply to AI colleagues and native-AI workplaces?”

Sarah Franklin, the CEO of HR company Lattice, has more existential concerns. Lattice added digital employees to the org chart two years ago, before the concept had fully entered the mainstream. Franklin emphasizes that Lattice uses this model to encourage accountability—not to encourage workers to treat AI colleagues as if they were human.

Franklin sees such anthropomorphizing as a strategy by tech companies to get users hooked on their services, unable to resist the dopamine trigger of an emotional connection. While this can help companies build an active user base, Franklin believes it may have detrimental neurological and behavioral repercussions for the human workforce.

“We have these models that have consumed all human knowledge, and are so proud to have these multitrillion valuations—but are potentially destroying humanity,” Franklin says. “It is very scary. And what is the purpose? Is the purpose to put people out of work?”

# Digital coworkers: How AI agents are reshaping enterprise teams

**Across industries, a new type of employee is emerging: the digital coworker.**

[AI agents](https://www.datarobot.com/resources/the-enterprise-guide-to-agentic-ai/) that collaborate, learn, and make decisions are changing how enterprise teams operate and grow.

These aren’t like the static chatbots or RPA scripts running in the background. They’re autonomous agents that act as colleagues — not code — helping teams move faster, make smarter decisions, and scale institutional knowledge.

Managers are now learning to hire, onboard, and supervise AI agents like human employees, while teams are redefining trust, learning how to share context, and reshaping collaboration around intelligent systems that can act independently.

For leaders, this shift isn’t just about adopting new technology. It’s about transforming how organizations work and scale, and building more adaptive, resilient teams for the age of human-AI collaboration.

This post explores how AI leaders can guide trust, collaboration, and performance as digital coworkers become part of the workforce.

## **Key takeaways**

- **AI agents function as autonomous digital coworkers rather than traditional automation tools:** These agents can reason through problems, coordinate across departments, and make independent decisions without constant human supervision, fundamentally changing how enterprise teams operate.
- **Digital coworkers handle repetitive tasks while humans focus on strategic work:** AI agents manage analytical workloads, process monitoring, and routine decisions 24/7, allowing human employees to concentrate on creativity, strategy, and relationship-building activities.
- **Agent onboarding mirrors human onboarding but moves at a much faster rate:** Organizations introduce processes and gradually expand an AI agent’s responsibilities the same way they would with new employees, but the learning curve compresses from months to hours.
- **Trust development between humans and AI agents follows a predictable three-stage pattern:** Teams typically progress from initial skepticism to cautious testing on low-risk processes, eventually reaching collaborative confidence as agents consistently demonstrate reliable decision-making.
- **Early adopters gain competitive advantages through human-AI collaboration capabilities:** Organizations embracing digital coworkers build adaptive capacity and institutional knowledge that competitors struggle to replicate, creating sustainable operational differentiation.

## How AI agents are shifting from tools to digital coworkers

**AI agents** **acting as digital coworkers can reason through problems, coordinate across departments, and make decisions that directly influence outcomes.**

Unlike traditional rule-based automation tools, these digital colleagues have the autonomy and awareness to carry out complex tasks without constant human supervision.

Consider [supply chain operations](https://www.datarobot.com/blog/ai-in-supply-chain-a-trillion-dollar-opportunity/), for instance. In a “self-fulfilling” supply chain, an agent might:

- Monitor market conditions
- Detect disruptions
- Evaluate alternatives
- Negotiate vendor adjustments

And it can do it all without a human even glancing at their dashboard. Instead of chasing updates and keeping an eye on constant market fluctuations, the human role shifts to strategy.

For leaders, this shift redefines process efficiency and management itself. It completely changes what it means to assign responsibility, ensure accountability, and measure performance in a workforce that now includes intelligent systems.

## Why enterprises are embracing AI employees

**The rise of AI employees isn’t about chasing the latest technology trend — it’s about building a more resilient, adaptable workforce.**

Enterprises are under constant pressure to sustain performance, manage risk, and respond faster to change. Digital coworkers are emerging as a way to extend capacity and improve consistency in how teams operate.

AI agents can already take on analytical workloads, process monitoring, and repeatable decisions that slow teams down. In doing so, they help human employees focus on the work that requires creativity, strategy, and sound judgment.

For leadership teams, value shows up in measurable outcomes:

- **Greater productivity:** Agents handle repeatable tasks autonomously, 24/7, compounding efficiency across departments.
- **Operational resilience::** Continuous execution reduces bottlenecks and helps teams sustain performance through change.
- **Faster, data-driven decisions:** Agents analyze, simulate, and recommend actions in real time, giving leaders an information edge with less downtime.
- **Higher human impact:** Teams redirect their time toward creativity, strategy, and innovation.

Forward-looking organizations are already redesigning workflows around this partnership. In [finance](https://www.datarobot.com/blog/cash-flow-forecasting/), agents handle “lights-out lending” processes around the clock while human analysts refine models and validate results. In operations, they monitor supply chains and surface insights before risks escalate.

The result: a more responsive, data-driven enterprise where people and AI each focus on what they do best.

## Inside the partnership between humans and AI coworkers

**Think about the process of** **onboarding** **a new** **team member** **: You introduce processes, show how systems connect, and gradually increase responsibility. Agent** **onboarding** **follows that same pattern, except the learning curve is measured in hours — not months.**

Over time, the agent + employee partnership evolves. Agents handle the repeatable and time-sensitive (monitoring data flows, coordinating across systems, keeping decisions moving), while humans focus on creative, strategic, and relationship-driven work that requires context and judgment.

Let’s go back to the supply chain example above. In [supply chain management](https://www.datarobot.com/resources/how-agentic-ai-transforms-the-supply-chain-lifecycle/), AI agents monitor demand signals, adjust inventory, and coordinate vendors automatically, while human leaders focus on long-term resilience and supplier strategy. That division of work turns human _oversight_ into _orchestration_ and gives teams the freedom (and time) to operate proactively instead of reactively.

This collaboration model is redefining how teams communicate, assign responsibility, and measure success, setting the stage for deeper cultural shifts.

## The culture shift: Working with digital teammates

[Cultural adaptation to digital coworkers](https://www.datarobot.com/resources/close-5-gaps-to-succeed-in-your-ai-agent-adoption/) follows a predictable pattern, but the timeline varies depending on how teams manage the change. Skepticism is normal early on as employees question how much they should trust automated decisions or delegate responsibility to agents. But over time, as AI coworkers prove reliable and transparent in their actions, teams feel more confident in them and collaboration starts to feel natural.

**The initial hurdle often centers on trust and control.** Human teams are used to knowing who’s responsible for what, how decisions get made, and where to go when problems arise. Digital agents introduce a new and unfamiliar element where some decisions happen automatically, processes run without human oversight, and coordination occurs between systems instead of people.

This “trust curve” typically:

- **Starts with skepticism:** “Can this agent really handle complex tasks and decisions?”
- **Moves through cautious testing:** “Let’s see how it performs on lower-risk processes.”
- **Reaches collaborative confidence:** “This agent consistently makes good decisions faster than we could.”

But what happens when agents disagree with human decisions, or when their recommendations go against “the way we’ve always done it”?

These are actually a blessing in disguise, and are opportunities where humans need to weigh competing agent recommendations.

It’s in these moments that hidden assumptions in your processes might surface, revealing potentially better approaches that neither humans nor agents would have discovered on their own. And the final solution might involve human expertise, agent automation, or a healthy combination of both.

## Preparing for the next phase of human + AI collaboration

Moving from traditional teams to human-agent collaboration offers operational improvement and a competitive differentiation that can grow over time. Early adopters are already building organizational capabilities that competitors will struggle to replicate as they play catch-up.

AI agents are the digital employees that can learn your business context, [maintain governance](https://www.datarobot.com/blog/ai-governance-solutions/), streamline your processes, and develop institutional knowledge that stays in-house.

With agents handling more operational duties, human teams can focus on innovation, strategy, and relationship building. This gives you breathing room on growth, using the resources you already have. Organizations that embrace digital coworkers are building adaptive capacity for future challenges we can’t even anticipate (yet).

**Discover how** [**AI leaders**](https://www.datarobot.com/why-datarobot/leaders/) **are preparing their organizations for the agent workforce future.**

## **Frequently asked questions**

**What is a digital AI agent in enterprise teams?** A digital AI agent is an autonomous software system that acts as a coworker by monitoring conditions, making decisions, and coordinating tasks across departments without constant human supervision, unlike traditional chatbots or rule-based automation.

**What are the main capabilities of AI agents as digital coworkers?** AI agents can reason through problems, evaluate alternatives, negotiate adjustments, and execute complex workflows 24/7 while maintaining governance and learning business context over time.

**How do AI agents differ from traditional automation tools?** AI agents have autonomy and awareness to carry out complex tasks independently, while traditional automation follows fixed rules and requires human oversight for each decision point.

**What is the trust curve when adopting AI digital coworkers?** Teams typically start with skepticism about automated decisions, move through cautious testing on lower-risk processes, and reach collaborative confidence once agents consistently demonstrate reliable performance faster than manual methods.

10 Best AI Coworkers in 2026: Reviewed & Compared

[← All articles](https://www.vellum.ai/blog)

Copy page

## Quick Overview

An AI coworker works alongside you throughout your actual workday. Not a chatbot you open, ask something, and close. Something that has context about your work, connects to your tools, reaches out when something needs attention, and contributes without waiting to be asked. This guide covers the 10 best AI coworker tools in 2026, who each one is built for, and where each one falls short.

## Top 10 AI Coworkers Shortlist

- [Vellum](https://www.vellum.ai/): A personal AI assistant with persistent memory, credential isolation, and a proactive outreach engine that works across desktop, iOS, web, Slack, and Telegram.
- [Viktor](https://getviktor.com/): A Slack-native AI coworker built on Zeta Labs' agent infrastructure, with 3,000+ integrations, weeks-long context retention, and its own cloud computer per workspace.
- [Claude Cowork](https://coworkerai.io/): Anthropic's desktop AI that executes multi-step tasks autonomously in an isolated VM with file access and computer use.
- [Perplexity Computer](https://www.perplexity.ai/): A cloud-based agentic assistant that spins up parallel sub-agents for complex research and multi-part tasks simultaneously.
- [Microsoft 365 Copilot](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot): Microsoft's AI embedded across Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, and the entire M365 ecosystem.
- [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.im/): An open-source agent harness with 24+ channels, full local execution, and MIT licensing.

## Why I Wrote This

The term "AI coworker" is getting applied to everything from Slack chatbots to full autonomous agents. Most products using the label are actually productivity chatbots with a few integrations bolted on. A real AI coworker has context about how you work, knows your tools, and contributes without being prompted each time you open it. I tested and reviewed 10 tools that claim the label to find the ones that actually function as a working presence alongside you, not just a smarter search box.

## What Are AI Coworkers?

An AI coworker is an AI system designed to work alongside you throughout the workday. Unlike a chatbot that responds to one-off prompts, a true AI coworker has persistent memory of your work and context, connects to your actual tools, and takes action on your behalf without being prompted each time. The personal AI assistant market is valued at $4.84 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach $19.63 billion by 2030, growing at a 41.9% CAGR. [\[1\]](https://www.vellum.ai/blog/best-personal-ai-assistants-2026) The fastest-growing segment within that market is agentic AI: tools that act, not just respond.

### Key 2026 Trends in AI Coworkers

- Agentic AI is entering daily work. Stanford HAI's 2026 AI Index identifies "sharp acceleration in agentic AI deployment" as a defining theme for the year, with autonomous systems moving from pilots into real workflows. [\[2\]](https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026)
- Persistent memory is now expected. In 2025, cross-session memory was a differentiating feature. In 2026, it is close to a baseline requirement. Every serious contender now ships some form of user-level memory, from stored preferences to full personal knowledge bases.
- Multi-surface presence matters more. Users increasingly expect AI to follow them across devices and apps rather than requiring a context switch every time they change tools.
- Credential security is becoming a real selection criterion. As AI coworkers get access to email, calendars, and financial accounts, how tools handle credentials is no longer a footnote. It is a core architecture decision.
- Gallup reports frequent AI use at work grew from 19% to 23% of workers in a single quarter in 2025. [\[3\]](https://thenetworkinstallers.com/blog/ai-in-the-workplace-statistics/) Early adopters in the coworker category are pulling significantly ahead of peers.

## What Is Missing From Most AI Coworker Tools?

- Context resets after each session, so you re-explain your work every time you open the tool
- No proactive behavior — they wait to be asked instead of surfacing what matters
- Single-surface access — only usable from one app or one device
- Credential exposure — API keys and tokens stored in files the AI model can read
- No persistent identity — the AI has no presence in your tools, only a browser tab
- Integration breadth without depth — hundreds of connections that do shallow things

## Who Needs an AI Coworker?

- Founders and operators running cross-functional work who need something that stays on top of email, Slack, and follow-ups without constant prompting
- Remote and async teams coordinating across time zones who want an always-on AI that monitors inbound and surfaces what needs attention
- Knowledge workers — researchers, strategists, writers — who move across many sources and surfaces without wanting to lose context between sessions
- Developers who want an agent handling admin work and communication while they focus on building
- Busy professionals spending more time managing their inbox and calendar than doing actual work

## What to Look for in an AI Coworker

- Persistent memory across sessions and surfaces
- Proactive reach-outs without being asked
- Deep integration into email, calendar, Slack, and code tools
- Credential security where tokens never reach the AI model
- Multi-surface presence: desktop, mobile, messaging channels
- A clear identity layer: the AI has its own accounts and working presence
- Configurable trust settings you control
- Fast setup — useful in minutes, not after days of configuration

## Our Review Process

Each tool was evaluated on five criteria weighted by how much they affect whether the tool actually functions as a coworker versus a chatbot:

- Memory and context persistence — 30%
- Integration depth and action capability — 25%
- Credential security — 20%
- Multi-surface availability — 15%
- Setup speed and accessibility — 10%

Pricing was verified against each vendor's website at time of writing. No affiliate links. No sponsored placements.

## Best AI Coworkers (2026)

### 1\. Vellum

[Vellum](https://www.vellum.ai/) is a personal AI assistant built to work alongside you throughout the day, with persistent memory, credential isolation by architecture, and a proactive engine that reaches out when something needs attention.

Score: 100

Standout strengths:

- Memory persists across every surface and every session — context you build in the morning is available when you return in the evening
- Credential isolation is architectural: your API keys and tokens live in a separate process and never reach the AI model itself, which means a compromised prompt cannot leak your credentials
- The proactivity engine runs on its own schedule, flagging stale follow-ups, surfacing calendar items, and reaching out before you ask
- Available as a native desktop app, iOS app, and web app, plus Slack and Telegram, all sharing the same persistent memory
- Your assistant can have its own email address, its own accounts, and its own working presence in your tools — it acts on your behalf without impersonating you
- Skills system lets you install new capabilities from a catalog or build custom ones as your workflow expands

Trade-offs:

- Memory and context improve significantly with continued use — the experience in week three is meaningfully better than day one
- Specialized integrations require initial setup to configure correctly

Pricing: Free download. Cloud hosting available.

Compared to other AI coworkers: Vellum is the only tool in this list with credential isolation built into the architecture rather than bolted on. Every other option stores credentials in config files or cloud infrastructure accessible to the model layer. If your AI coworker has access to your email, financial accounts, and code repositories, that distinction carries real weight. The proactivity engine also sets it apart from every other tool here — most AI coworkers wait for you to open them. Vellum checks in on its own cycle and reaches out when something is unfinished or urgent.

* * *

### 2\. Viktor

[Viktor](https://getviktor.com/) is a Slack-native AI coworker built on Zeta Labs' autonomous agent infrastructure, with 3,000+ integrations, a persistent cloud computer per workspace, and weeks-long context retention across your team's workflows.

Score: 91

Standout strengths:

- Lives natively in Slack (with Microsoft Teams support coming), so the entire team can interact with it without installing anything additional
- 3,000+ integrations let Viktor take action across Stripe, HubSpot, Google Ads, GitHub, Linear, Notion, and more directly from a Slack conversation
- Maintains context across weeks-long projects, coordinating people and deadlines without losing thread
- Proactively monitors your team's workflows, spots problems like a CPA spike before anyone notices, and proposes automations rather than just sending alerts
- 12,000+ workspaces as of May 2026, with a 5.0/5 Product Hunt rating on launch
- SOC 2 Type 1 certified, with Type 2 and ISO 27001 in progress; data never used for model training

Trade-offs:

- Fully cloud-based — your workflow context lives on Viktor's infrastructure
- Credit-based pricing means heavy users can exceed the base plan; heavy workflows can run $300–$400/month in reported usage from power users

Pricing: Free (Starter — $100 one-time credits). Team $50/month per Slack workspace (20,000 monthly credits). Enterprise custom.

Compared to Claude Cowork: Viktor is the stronger pick when your work happens inside Slack and you need team-wide integration across your business stack. Claude Cowork is better for individual desktop task execution where you want local file access and Anthropic-quality reasoning on complex documents.

* * *

### 3\. Claude Cowork

[Claude Cowork](https://coworkerai.io/) is Anthropic's desktop AI that went generally available on April 9, 2026, bringing multi-step autonomous task execution inside an isolated VM to macOS and Windows.

Score: 87

Standout strengths:

- Plans and executes complex multi-step tasks in parallel, breaking projects into sub-tasks and running them autonomously
- Runs inside an isolated VM with controlled file and network access — documents and data stay local during execution
- Computer use capability: reads your screen, navigates your desktop, and takes actions in any app the same way a person would
- Available on both macOS and Windows with full feature parity
- Powered by Claude Opus 4.7, optimized for long-horizon agentic reasoning

Trade-offs:

- No cross-session persistent memory: Cowork resets context between standalone sessions and does not build a cumulative model of you over time
- Task allocation is opaque — you cannot estimate how much of your plan a complex task will consume before starting

Pricing: Requires a Claude subscription. Pro $20/month. Team $30/user/month. Max $100–$200/month.

Compared to Perplexity Computer: Claude Cowork is the stronger option for document-heavy and desktop task execution that requires Anthropic's reasoning quality. Perplexity Computer is better for web-grounded research workflows where parallel sub-agents and real-time information access are the priority.

* * *

### 4\. Perplexity Computer

[Perplexity Computer](https://www.perplexity.ai/) is Perplexity's cloud-based agentic assistant that spins up parallel sub-agents to handle complex, multi-part tasks simultaneously.

Score: 82

Standout strengths:

- Parallel sub-agent architecture breaks large tasks into pieces and routes each to specialized models, completing multi-part research faster than sequential tools
- Web-grounded by design: draws on real-time search results for every task, so answers reflect current information rather than training data
- Accessible from any device with no local setup required
- Strong on research-intensive workflows: competitive analysis, market research, document synthesis

Trade-offs:

- Credit-metered for complex tasks — costs are hard to predict before starting a run
- No persistent identity or memory across sessions: each task starts fresh with no accumulated context

Pricing: Included in Perplexity Pro at $20/month.

Compared to Microsoft 365 Copilot: Perplexity Computer wins on research quality and web grounding for any topic. Microsoft 365 Copilot wins if your actual work lives in Office apps, SharePoint, and Teams, where its native integration eliminates context switching entirely.

* * *

### 5\. Microsoft 365 Copilot

[Microsoft 365 Copilot](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot) is Microsoft's AI assistant embedded across Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, PowerPoint, and the rest of the M365 suite.

Score: 79

Standout strengths:

- Native to the M365 ecosystem: drafts in Word, builds Excel formulas, summarizes Teams meetings, and triages Outlook without switching tools
- Organization-wide context: can access shared documents, meeting transcripts, and email threads within your M365 environment
- Enterprise compliance controls: audit logs, data residency, and GDPR-ready infrastructure included
- Monthly active agent counts across M365 growing year-over-year per Microsoft's telemetry data

Trade-offs:

- Requires a Microsoft 365 subscription plus the Copilot add-on at $30/user/month — expensive for small teams or individual users
- Value is significantly limited if your work does not already live in the M365 stack

Pricing: $30/user/month add-on to Microsoft 365 Business or Enterprise.

Compared to OpenClaw: Microsoft 365 Copilot wins for enterprise teams already embedded in Microsoft's ecosystem. OpenClaw is the better choice for developers and technical users who want free, local, multi-channel execution without platform lock-in.

* * *

### 6\. OpenClaw

[OpenClaw](https://openclaw.im/) is an open-source agent harness with 24+ integration channels, full local execution, and a community of developers that is the largest of any open-source agent project.

Score: 75

Standout strengths:

- 24+ supported channels including Telegram, Slack, Discord, Gmail, Linear, and GitHub — broader channel coverage than any other open-source tool
- MIT licensed and free to self-host at any scale with no per-seat pricing
- Runs entirely on your machine by default — data stays local
- Highly extensible plugin ecosystem for adding capabilities without modifying core code
- 370,000+ GitHub stars, active community governance following founder's departure to OpenAI

Trade-offs:

- Credentials live in a config file with model-level access — the project's own SECURITY.md notes that prompt injection attacks are out of scope
- Community governance means release cadence can be inconsistent

Pricing: Free (self-hosted). Cloud hosting option available.

Compared to ChatGPT: OpenClaw gives local execution, channel breadth, and zero ongoing cost. ChatGPT gives the most familiar interface, strongest general ecosystem, and no self-hosting overhead. If you are comfortable running a local agent, OpenClaw is the better value. If you want a managed experience, ChatGPT is easier.

* * *

### 7\. ChatGPT

[ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/) is OpenAI's conversational AI with Operator for browser automation, Deep Research for long-horizon analysis, and Workspace Agents (launched April 2026) for persistent team-level workflows.

Score: 72

Standout strengths:

- Workspace Agents bring persistent AI agents into team workflows with shared context and recurring task support
- Operator handles browser-based tasks including form filling, bookings, and price lookups autonomously
- The most widely used AI tool in most companies' existing stacks, with over 800 million weekly active users globally as of mid-2025
- GPT-5.5 Instant supports 128K context windows for large document work

Trade-offs:

- No persistent identity layer: ChatGPT does not have its own email, accounts, or presence in your tools
- Reactive by default — it waits for you to open it

Pricing: Free tier available. Plus $20/month. Team $30/user/month. Enterprise custom.

Compared to Asana AI Teammates: ChatGPT is the better general-purpose AI coworker for individuals with unstructured workflows. Asana AI Teammates are better when work is structured inside Asana with clear owners, deadlines, and project context.

* * *

### 8\. Asana AI Teammates

[Asana AI Teammates](https://asana.com/) are collaborative agents embedded in Asana's Work Graph that progress work, nudge owners on overdue items, and update project statuses without human prompting.

Score: 68

Standout strengths:

- Deep integration with Asana's Work Graph: understands project dependencies, owners, and timelines natively
- Proactively flags blockers, escalates missed deadlines, and suggests next steps within your actual project structure
- No-code AI Studio for building or customizing AI teammates without developer involvement
- Genuinely useful for cross-functional teams coordinating complex, multi-owner launches

Trade-offs:

- Almost all value is limited to Asana users — minimal reach if your work does not live in Asana
- Requires Advanced plan ($24.99/user/month) or higher

Pricing: Included in Asana Advanced at $24.99/user/month (billed annually). Business $30.49/user/month.

Compared to Gumloop: Asana AI Teammates are more purpose-built for structured project workflows with clear owners. Gumloop is better for teams that want to build and share custom agents that work across multiple apps without being tied to one PM tool.

* * *

### 9\. Gumloop

[Gumloop](https://www.gumloop.com/) is a cloud AI agent platform for building, sharing, and running multi-app workflow automation agents across your team's tool stack.

Score: 65

Standout strengths:

- LLM-agnostic: supports Claude, GPT, Gemini, and open-source models depending on the task
- Agents and workflows can be built once and shared across an entire team
- Gumstack security layer includes tool call traceability, role-based access control, MCP inventory auditing, and SSO/SCIM support
- 1,000+ integrations including Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, HubSpot, and Salesforce

Trade-offs:

- Requires meaningful setup time — you build the automation flows yourself rather than getting a ready-to-use coworker
- Does not proactively manage your day; it runs the automations you have configured

Pricing: Team $138/month (includes 10 users and 2,000 AI credits). Enterprise custom.

Compared to Notion AI Agent: Gumloop is better for teams building multi-app agents others can use across the stack. Notion AI Agent is stronger if your knowledge and work already live primarily in Notion.

* * *

### 10\. Notion AI Agent

[Notion AI Agent](https://www.notion.so/) is Notion's built-in AI capability that lets teams automate recurring tasks, answer questions from their knowledge base, and run agents on schedules or triggers.

Score: 62

Standout strengths:

- Natively embedded in Notion pages and databases — no context switching or integration setup for Notion-centric teams
- Custom Agents connect to Slack, Calendar, and external tools via MCP
- Answers questions from your actual team documentation rather than generic training data
- Included in most paid Notion tiers at no additional charge

Trade-offs:

- Value is limited to teams with Notion as their primary workspace
- Agent capabilities are narrower than dedicated AI coworker platforms

Pricing: Notion AI included in Plus ($12/user/month) and Business ($18/user/month) plans.

Compared to Vellum: Notion AI Agent is useful in-workspace AI for Notion users. Vellum runs independently of any single workspace, across every surface you use, with credential isolation, persistent memory, and a proactivity engine that operates whether or not you have Notion open.

* * *

## Why Vellum Stands Out

Most AI coworkers in 2026 are Slack integrations, desktop apps with good task execution, or chatbots with memory bolted on. Vellum is the only tool in this category that was designed from the start as a persistent presence across every surface you use.

## FAQs

### What is an AI coworker?

An AI coworker is an AI system designed to work alongside you throughout your workday, not just when you open a chat tab. It has persistent memory of your context, connects to your tools, and takes action on your behalf without being prompted each time.

### How is an AI coworker different from an AI chatbot?

A chatbot responds to prompts. An AI coworker has context that persists between sessions, connects to your actual tools, and in the best cases, reaches out proactively when something needs attention. Every session with a chatbot starts from zero.

### How is an AI coworker different from an AI employee?

AI employees are typically purpose-built for a specific role — an AI SDR, an AI software engineer, an AI customer support agent. An AI coworker is a general collaborating presence that works with you across the full breadth of how you work, rather than replacing one specialized function.

### What does a good AI coworker actually do?

The key capabilities: remembers context across sessions, connects to email and calendar and messaging tools, takes actions in those tools on your behalf, surfaces what needs attention without being asked, and follows you across devices and surfaces.

### Which AI coworker is best for individuals?

Vellum is the strongest pick for individuals who want a persistent AI presence that knows their context and works proactively. Viktor is the best option for individuals whose primary work surface is Slack and who need team-wide integration.

### Which AI coworker is best for teams?

Viktor stands out for Slack-native teams. Microsoft 365 Copilot is the strongest for enterprise teams in the M365 ecosystem. Asana AI Teammates are the best fit when work is structured in Asana projects.

### Are AI coworkers safe to use with sensitive data?

It depends on the tool and the architecture. Vellum uses credential isolation so API keys never reach the AI model. OpenClaw stores credentials in a local file. Viktor stores credentials in cloud infrastructure with enterprise-grade encryption. The right answer depends on your threat model and compliance requirements.

### Can AI coworkers replace human teammates?

Current AI coworkers augment human work rather than replace it. They handle high-volume, repeatable tasks — inbox triage, status updates, research, follow-ups — and free up time for the work that requires human judgment.

### Do AI coworkers work on mobile?

Vellum has a native iOS app with the same persistent memory as the desktop. Most other tools in this list are desktop or web-only, or accessible through mobile-responsive browser interfaces.

## **Customer Service: Deliver Faster, Smarter Support**

Imagine a customer reaching out to your support team to check the status of their order. Normally, this would require a customer service representative to manually search through multiple systems to locate the necessary information. With [customer service AI Agents](https://www.cm.com/support/), this process becomes seamless. The AI agent can instantly access backend systems, retrieve the order details, and provide the customer with a real-time update, whether it’s a tracking link or delivery status.

AI Agents excel at handling repetitive, time-consuming tasks like these, freeing up your human employees to focus on more complex and meaningful customer interactions. For example, they can dedicate their time to offering in-depth product advice or providing personalized support to high-value customers. Instead of spending time searching for information, your customer service team can focus on solving unique issues, building relationships, and delivering exceptional service.

![halo-image-customer-service-nl](https://www.cm.com/cdn/web/nl-nl/halo-image-customer-service-nl.png)

## **Marketing: Create Personalized, Two-Way Conversations**

Traditional marketing campaigns often feel one-sided. You send out emails or ads, and customers passively consume the content. [Marketing AI Agents](https://www.cm.com/halo/) completely change this dynamic by enabling real-time, two-way conversations that are personal and engaging.

Imagine this: a customer signs up for your newsletter, and instead of a generic confirmation email, an AI Agent immediately starts a conversation. “Thanks for subscribing! Let‘s get to know each other. What kind of products are you most interested in?” This simple interaction not only helps you gather valuable customer insights but also makes the customer feel valued and understood.

AI Agents don’t stop there. They can proactively reach out to customers with personalized offers. For example, if a customer regularly buys a product, like coffee or office supplies, the agent can send a timely reminder when it’s time to reorder. If the customer has questions, the agent can handle them instantly, ensuring a seamless experience from marketing to conversion.

AI Agents are also powerful sales enablers. Acting as digital shopping assistants, they guide customers through the buying journey, just like a knowledgeable salesperson in a store.

Picture this: a customer messages your business on WhatsApp, “I’m looking for a new pair of running shoes.” The AI Agent analyzes the customer’s preferences, purchase history, and product availability to recommend the perfect pair. If the customer has questions about sizing or compatibility, the agent provides instant answers. It can even go a step further by adding the product to the customer’s cart or completing the purchase on their behalf. Moreover, cross sell can be stimulated by complementary product recommendations by the AI Agent.

By automating these interactions, AI Agents not only streamline the shopping experience but also boost the chances of conversion. At the same time, your sales team can focus on high-value opportunities, such as providing personalized product recommendations, nurturing long-term customer relationships, or managing key accounts. This approach ensures that both efficiency and customer satisfaction are optimized, allowing your team to deliver a more tailored and impactful service.

## **Operational: Automate the Routine, Focus on the Meaningful**

AI Agents aren’t just for customer-facing tasks. [Halo](https://www.cm.com/halo/) can also revolutionize your internal operations. Think about all the repetitive, time-consuming tasks your employees handle daily: logging hours, requesting vacation days, or navigating through HR systems. AI Agents can take these tasks off their plates, allowing your team to focus on the core of their work.

Take vacation requests, for example. Instead of logging into an HR system, an employee can simply message the AI Agent: “I’d like to take next Friday off.” The agent checks their remaining vacation balance, submits the request, and notifies their manager for approval—all within seconds.

Similarly, for time tracking, the agent can integrate with tools like Outlook to automatically log hours based on calendar events. At the end of the week, the AI Agent sends a summary for the employee to review and approve. No more tedious data entry, no more wasted time.

#### ![Appointment Agent Template](https://www.cm.com/cdn/web/en/appointmentagent-template-visual.png)

### **Multimodal Capabilities: Beyond Text, Into Visual Understanding**

AI Agents aren’t limited to text-based interactions. They can also process images, opening new possibilities for customer service and sales. For example, a customer can upload a photo of a product and ask, “Does this match the new jacket I’m considering?” The agent can analyze the image and provide a thoughtful recommendation.

This capability is particularly valuable in industries like fashion, electronics, or automotive, where visual context is often crucial. By understanding both text and images, AI Agents deliver a richer, more personalized experience.

### **A True Partnership Between Humans and AI**

One of the biggest misconceptions about AI is that it’s here to replace human employees. In reality, AI Agents are designed to complement your team, not compete with them. By taking over repetitive, low-value tasks, they free up your employees to focus on what they do best: solving complex problems, building relationships, and driving innovation. Additionally, human employees can take on new responsibilities, such as maintaining and fine-tuning the AI Agents, developing their capabilities, and ensuring continuous improvement. This not only enhances the AI’s performance but also provides growth opportunities for your team, empowering them to expand their skill sets and take on more strategic roles.

Think of it this way: when you hire a new colleague, you don’t expect them to do everything. You assign them specific tasks that align with their strengths. The same goes for AI Agents. By clearly defining their role, whether it’s handling customer inquiries, automating internal processes, or assisting with sales, you set them up for success. At the same time, your human team remains essential in monitoring quality, refining processes, and driving innovation, creating a more efficient, collaborative, and harmonious workplace.

### **Why AI Agents Are a Must-Have for Your Business**

The way you interact with customers, employees, and technology is evolving rapidly. Customer expectations are higher than ever, and with AI Agents, you can not only meet but exceed these demands. AI Agents are leading this transformation, providing a smarter, faster, and more personalized approach to conducting business and delivering value across every department.

However, their true power lies in how they empower your team. By taking over repetitive and time-consuming tasks, AI Agents enable your employees to focus on what truly matters: creating exceptional customer experiences, building meaningful relationships, closing critical deals, and driving innovation. This synergy between AI and human expertise ensures your organization stays agile, efficient, and customer-focused in an ever-changing landscape.

### **Ready to Welcome Your New Digital Colleague?**

Introducing an AI Agent doesn’t happen overnight. It’s similar to hiring a new team member: it requires thoughtful preparation and a well-defined plan.

Just as you would onboard a new colleague, you need to carefully integrate an AI Agent into your organization. This means clearly defining its role: What tasks will it take on? How will it support your team? who is responsible for managing and maintaining the AI Agent? Once its role is established, you’ll need to equip it with the right tools to succeed, such as access to relevant data, seamless integration with your existing systems, and clear guidelines for how it should function.

When the AI Agent is fully onboarded and operating smoothly, the benefits quickly become apparent. Your customers will experience faster, more personalized service, your employees will have more time to focus on meaningful and creative work, and your business will run more efficiently and effectively.

### **Take the First Step Toward Your AI-Powered Future**

Are you ready to take the next step? Together, we can create a future where technology and humanity work in harmony, delivering exceptional results and unlocking exciting new opportunities for growth. Whether you’re looking to streamline operations, enhance customer experiences, or empower your team, we’ll help you identify the best opportunities and guide you through implementation.

Contact us today and let’s shape a smarter, more efficient future together.

### What is an AI Employee?

An AI employee is an autonomous digital worker designed to execute specific business functions from start to finish. Unlike simple scripts or standard chatbots that rely on pre-programmed decision trees, AI employees utilize large language models, structured decision frameworks, and persistent memory to understand context, solve problems, and communicate naturally.

The distinction matters. A chatbot follows a script — it can answer an FAQ or route a ticket. An AI employee owns the outcome. When a customer writes in about a billing error, an AI employee like Raya reads the full conversation history, pulls up the account in your CRM, identifies the discrepancy, processes the correction, and responds to the customer in their preferred language — all without a human touching the ticket.

AI employees operate across three core business functions today: customer service (handling support tickets, phone calls, and live chat), sales (prospecting, qualifying leads, booking meetings, and following up), and recruiting (screening resumes, conducting interviews, and scoring candidates). Each function requires a different skill set, decision framework, and integration stack — which is why Teammates.ai built three specialized AI employees rather than one generic assistant.

The term 'AI employee' reflects a fundamental shift in how businesses think about work. Instead of buying software licenses per seat, companies hire AI employees that deliver outcomes — tickets resolved, leads qualified, candidates screened. The unit of value is the job done, not the tool accessed.

### How AI Employees Differ from Automation

Traditional automation platforms like Zapier or Make move data from Point A to Point B based on strict if-this-then-that rules. They work well for predictable, linear workflows. If an exception occurs — an unexpected input, an edge case, a customer request that doesn't fit the template — the automation breaks and requires human intervention.

AI employees possess cognitive flexibility that automation fundamentally lacks. When faced with an ambiguous customer request, an AI employee reasons through the problem. It considers context from previous interactions, weighs multiple possible responses, and selects the approach most likely to resolve the issue. If it can't resolve the situation within its defined authority, it escalates with full context so the human agent picks up without the customer repeating anything.

Consider a concrete example: a customer emails saying 'I'm frustrated with my order.' A Zapier automation sees keywords and routes to a support queue. Raya reads the full message, checks order history, identifies that the shipment was delayed, cross-references with the logistics provider's tracking data, processes a shipping credit, and responds empathetically — in Arabic, English, or any of 50+ languages.

The difference extends to learning. Automation rules are static — they do exactly what you programmed, forever. AI employees learn from every interaction. Raya monitors conversations for questions she can't fully answer, identifies knowledge gaps, and flags them for your team. Over time, her resolution rate climbs without manual retraining. This is what Teammates.ai calls Knowledge Intelligence — a self-healing knowledge base that gets smarter every day.

Another critical difference: automation handles tasks, AI employees handle jobs. A task is 'send a follow-up email after 3 days.' A job is 'qualify this inbound lead, research their company, personalize outreach based on their tech stack and pain points, send a multi-channel sequence, handle objections, and book a meeting.' Adam handles the entire job.

# Virtual Teammates vs AI agents: What's the difference?

![Leah Messenger](https://images2.cmp.optimizely.com/Zz1iMTI5MWIzNjQ0OTcxMWYxYWEwOTY2MzQ0ZTNjNGQwOQ==)Leah Messenger

Aug 17, 2026

There is a massive a big gap between a tool that waits for you to tell it what to do, and teammate who is already working when you open your laptop.

But as the martech landscape floods with "agentic" hype, the line between these two concepts is getting intentionally blurred by vendors. Every chatbot has rebranded as an agent, and every agent claims to be a "teammate".

It is creating a _major_ credibility gap. Marketers are being promised autonomous coworkers, but what they are actually getting are disconnected utilities that require constant babysitting, prompting, and correcting.\*

To build an agentic operating model that actually delivers results, you need to know exactly what you're deploying. So here's the real breakdown: standalone AI agents versus [Optimizely's Virtual Teammates](https://www.optimizely.com/solutions/virtual-teammates) (yep, _real_ virtual teammates), side by side.

###### \*This is _no joke_, we did the math in our recent **Global AI and Marketing Data Study**: [**76%**](https://www.optimizely.com/field-notes/guides/optimizely-2026-global-study) of marketers spend over 3 hours a week fixing AI output, with **5%** using over 7 disconnected tools in that time too.

## The structural breakdown

This isn't just a semantic pivot. It's a real difference in architecture, security, and execution. Standalone AI agents handle isolated, one-off tasks. Workflow agents handle more complex tasks that require some multiplayer action. Virtual Teammates hold down ongoing, collaborative roles.

In fact, [Virtual Teammates](https://www.optimizely.com/optimization-glossary/virtual-teammates) are made up of specialized agents, workflow agents, tools, and skills, bundled up into a real identity that can be customized and given personalities. And guess what? They're ready and waiting to take on expert tasks like no AI has done before.

Here's how they stack up across 10 specs that actually matter to a marketing org:

|  | ### Standalone AI agents | ### Optimizely's Virtual Teammates |
| **Identity and presence** | No persistent identity. A temporary session you open, prompt, and close. | First-class OptiID user. Shows up in your team roster, workload views, and audit logs. |
| **Access rights** | Shared-everything API credentials or single bot logins. | Individually scoped permissions per Virtual Teammate. |
| **Initiation model** | Works based on a strict input -> output model. You put in a specific input to get a specific output. | Proactive. Acts with or without a prompt, with ongoing collaborative interactions with humans and other virtual teammates in order to complete a task. |
| **Memory scope** | Starts fresh every session. | Persistent long-term memory. Org-specific information, previous work, and past decisions compound over time. |
| **Setup and deployment** | Depending on the vendor, this could require a range of  knowledge, from basics of agent building to more technical concepts or coding for configuration. | Ready to use out-of-the-box with plain-English  customization and pre-built role templates. |
| **Collaboration** | Single-player. Sequential handoffs. | Multiplayer. Humans and Virtual Teammates collaborate in parallel inside shared workspaces. |
| **Meeting presence** | Not applicable. Cannot participate in live sessions. | Meetings: full real-time participation. Teams/Slack: transcript-based summary & actions. |
| **Product** **access** | Isolated. Can requires complex API integrations to touch your core content systems, unless using Optimizely's agents that are native to the platforms you're using. | Native. Built straight into Optimizely Content Marketing Platform, CMS, and Experimentation  instances. |
| **Bottom line impact** | Hard to track. Shows up in soft, "productivity reports" at best. | Shows up in the headcount model, pipeline metrics, and growth. Real P&L visibility. |
| **Primary use case** | On-demand tasks: drafting copy, quick QA, rapid lookups, simple translations. | Ongoing roles: proactive auditing, campaign coordination, always-on optimization. |

## Virtual Teammates vs AI agents: The deep dive

🥽 Goggles on, we're diving into the key differentiators between a Virtual Teammate and an AI agent (so you can correct the people talking about any AI in a "teammate" way).

1

**Identity vs. Utility**

A standalone AI agent is a utility. When you run a prompt in ChatGPT, Claude, or a browser extension, you're interacting with an   engine that has no permanent place in your organization.

A Virtual Teammate has a real identity. They're provisioned as real users, so you manage them through your Admin Center exactly like human employees. They show up in your team lists, get assigned specific workflow steps in a campaign, and have their own company email addresses.

When a Virtual Teammate publishes a page in your CMS or moves a task to 'Approved,' the platform's audit trail records their name — not 'System Update' or 'API Token,' but 'Bubs' or 'Kara the Content Creator.' Whatever you choose.

2

**Shared credentials vs. Scoped permissions**

The biggest hurdle for enterprise AI adoption is security.

Virtual Teammates operate on a zero-trust, role-based access control (RBAC) model instead. Because they're individual users, you set their permissions in plain English: give a Virtual Teammate access to draft CMS pages but block them from publishing, or let them query audience segments in [Optimizely Data Platform](https://www.optimizely.com/products/data-platform) while restricting sensitive customer identifiers. If a Virtual Teammate's role gets retired, their access is revoked automatically via SCIM, just like offboarding an employee.

3

**Reactive prompts vs. Proactive execution**

Traditional AI is passive. It's a digital waiting room of tools hoping for a prompt, and if your team is busy, on vacation, or just forgets to log in, the tool sits entirely dark. The human is always the starting gun.

Virtual Teammates are proactive by default. They run on schedules, webhook triggers, email channels, and system events, so they don't need you to ask them to check last night's campaign metrics. While you're offline, a Virtual Teammate can:

- Scan your active CMS pages, detect content decay, flag gaps, and stage optimizations
- Compile a four-sentence digest of overnight changes and drop it in your Slack
- Monitor an ongoing experiment and raise an immediate flag if it detects sample ratio mismatch (SRM)

They don't need you to start the work. They're already running.

## Where to apply each model

This is not an all-or-nothing trade-off. Standalone AI agents and Virtual Teammates both have distinct, valuable places in a modern marketing organization. The trap is trying to solve a structural workflow problem with an on-demand tool.

![Virtual Teammate vs AI agent.png](https://images2.cmp.optimizely.com/Zz04OGQ1NmU2NDkxOGIxMWYxODFjMDFlY2FkMjVkZTY5MQ==?checkExpiry=false)

### When to use standalone AI agents:

arrow\_forward

**One-off drafting:** Writing a quick social caption variation or brainstorming headline angles for an ad.

arrow\_forward

**Transactional cleanups:** Formatting a messy raw CSV file or generating a quick schema markup block.

arrow\_forward

**On-demand search:** Asking an LLM to summarize a long industry report or pull a specific competitive fact.

arrow\_forward

**Regular automations (via workflow agents)**: Pull traffic or campaign data and email a report to key stakeholders every Monday morning.

### When to deploy Virtual Teammates:

arrow\_forward

**Continuous responsibilities:** Managing your weekly internal translation queue, running daily SEO/GEO audits, or continuously monitoring campaign health.

arrow\_forward

**Structured collaboration:** Roles that require side-by-side work with humans inside workflows — like a Chief of Staff pre-sorting briefs or a Conversion Optimizer setting up test variants.

arrow\_forward

**Strategic continuity:** Workflows where having a long-term memory of past team decisions, feedback loops, and brand voice is the difference between a high-quality asset and generic AI filler.

## Moving past the productivity metric

Measuring AI success in "hours saved" is the standard, but really... it's more of a defensive play. It satisfies no one above the director level for long, and it fails to show up on the company's balance sheet.

Virtual Teammates shift the conversation from capacity change to capability change.

Because they function as real headcount, they let you scale what your team can get done without stretching your people thin or adding operational overhead. You are not just giving your marketers a better calculator; you are giving them the team they actually need to execute their best ideas.

The marketing org chart is changing. The teams that win will not be the ones with the most tools in their drawer, but the ones with the most capable Virtual Teammates on their roster.

# AI agents as colleagues: the workplace design nobody’s planning for

[Feature](https://www.businessthink.unsw.edu.au/categories/feature) \| 1 April 2026

AI agents are reshaping enterprise work. This important shift requires a new kind of leadership on issues such as governance, risk and collaboration design

Noa \| Listen to news

Listen to this article

00:00  /  17:31

Listen to this article
